business: Site Manager: a venue website the owner runs by chatting with an AI agent
by_segment: Bar or bistro owner with a kitchen (1 location, changing menu)
Small café or coffee bar owner (1 location, under 10 staff)
by_behaviour: Relies on Google and delivery apps
why_not: My customers find me on Instagram and Facebook, and I already post the specials there myself for free. Paying 25 euros a month for a website nobody looks at, on a margin like mine, makes no sense.
My guests find me on Instagram and Google Maps, I already post the specials there for free. I raised prices twice this year, I'm not adding 25 € a month for a website nobody opens.

I already bleed money on POS, accounting and the delivery apps, and my lunch special goes on the board and on Facebook for free. Another 25 € plus VAT every month to an AI I can't phone when it breaks is not something I sign up for from an ad.

I don't buy things from an ad or an app I've never heard of. My daughter does the Instagram and that's enough for now; if another café owner I know used this and told me it works, maybe, but not from a stranger.

My whole day runs on Viber voice notes, with staff, suppliers, everyone. I'm not installing WhatsApp or Telegram just to talk to my website, and if it's not where I already am, I'll forget it exists within a week, like the old site.

I already have a site and my manager updates the menu when it matters; moving everything to a new site for 25 euros a month is a hassle I don't need right now. Most of my customers see us on Glovo and Google anyway.

I already pay for POS, accounting and give the delivery apps their cut, and I raised my prices twice this year. Another 25 a month, 30 with VAT, for a menu page I can fix on Facebook and Google myself is money I don't have spare right now.
why_yes: My lunch special changes every single day and right now it never makes it onto my site, so sending a photo of the board from my phone and tapping once is exactly the kind of thing I'd try. I'd start on one venue for a month, keep my old site running alongside, and point the table QR at this.

My lunch special changes every day and right now the website is always wrong, so sending a voice note I'm already used to and tapping once is exactly how I'd want to do it. 25 a month is less than one slow lunch service, so I'll try it for a month and cancel if it messes up.
flip: If one message from Viber updated my Instagram, Facebook and Google listing at the same time, so it saved me time instead of adding another thing to feed.
A free first month, plus it also updates my Google listing hours and menu, and a promise in writing that if I cancel I keep my domain and get my site and menu exported.
If one message also updated my Google Maps hours and menu and posted the special to Instagram, not just the website.
A local person who sets it up with me in the restaurant, a phone number that answers in Bulgarian, and a first month free so I can see if it actually saves me time.
Another café owner in Sofia I know shows me it on their phone, tells me it never got a price wrong, and there's a real person who speaks Bulgarian I can call.
Viber support, so I can send it a voice note in the same app I use all day.
If the same WhatsApp message also updated my prices, hours and specials on Google Maps, Glovo and Wolt, without me having to move off my current site.
My existing domain connected on the 25 € plan, plus a written promise that if I cancel I get a full export of the site and menu that I can host elsewhere.
If it worked on top of my existing site without moving anything and my manager could do it from Viber, with a free first month to see it actually saves time.
If it worked with the site I already have instead of making me move, and the first months were free so I could see it actually saves me time on the daily special.
My manager sets it up, uses it for a month on a free trial without bothering me, and I can see it actually brought in tables or saved us phone calls.
If the same WhatsApp message also updated my hours and menu on Google Maps and Glovo/Wolt, and there was a Bulgarian person I could phone when something goes wrong.
If it worked through Viber and also pushed the same update to my Instagram and Facebook and Google listing in one message, so it saves me time instead of adding another thing.
If it worked on Viber, so I could just send it a voice note the same way I message my supplier, and someone set it up for me in person.
Another café owner I know telling me they use it, it really works by just messaging, and the person behind it setting it up for me face to face.
If the same WhatsApp message also updated my menu and prices on Glovo, Wolt and Google Maps at once, then I'd pay, because that is the work that eats my time.
If the same message also updated my Instagram and Facebook, so I don't do the work twice, and I saw real customers in Sofia using the table QR menu.
If it also fixed my Google page and Glovo menu from the same message, and someone I know with a café showed me it working for a few months without mistakes, maybe I try the 15 euro plan.
